questions.question: Pearl Towers is taller than Sky Towers but shorter than Unity Towers. Unity Towers and Cyber Towers are of the same height. Pearl Towers is shorter than Indus Towers. Among the aforementioned buildings, which is the second shortest?
questions.questionHtml: Pearl Towers is taller than Sky Towers but shorter than Unity Towers. Unity Towers and Cyber Towers are of the same height. Pearl Towers is shorter than Indus Towers. Among the aforementioned buildings, which is the second shortest?
questions.solution:
Pearl Towers is taller than Sky Towers but shorter than Unity Towers,

Unity Towers > Pearl Towers > Sky Towers

Unity Towers and Cyber Towers are of the same height,

Unity Towers = Cyber Towers

Pearl Towers is shorter than Indus Towers,

Pearl Towers < Indus Towers

The possible final arrangement:

Cyber Towers = Unity Towers > Indus Tower > Pearl Towers > Sky Towers

Or

Indus Tower > Cyber Towers = Unity Towers > Pearl Towers > Sky Towers

Hence, in both cases, 'Pearl Towers' will be the second shortest.

Ozone is used for air purification at the crowded places. It is also used in sterilizing drinking water as it oxidizes all germs and bacteria.

questions.question: Two trains are moving in the same directions at speed of 43 km/h and 51 km/h respectively. The time taken by the faster train to cross a man sitting in the slower train is 72 seconds. What is the length (in metres) of the faster train?

questions.solution:
Given: The speed of 2 trains = 43 km/hr and 51 km/hr

Relative velocity of one train w.r.t. another = (51 - 43)km/hr = 8 km/hr

Relative velocity in m/s = 8 × (5/18) m/s

⇒ Distance covered by the train in 72 sec = 8 × (5/18) × 72 = 160

Since, this is the distance covered in crossing the man

Hence, the length of faster train = 160 m

questions.questionHtml: If \(x + \;\frac{1}{x} = 5\), then what is the value of \({x^5} + \frac{1}{{{x^5}}}?\)
questions.solution:
Given,

(x + 1/x) = 5

Squaring both sides

⇒ (x + 1/x)2 = 25

⇒ x2 + 1/x2 = 25 – 2 = 23       ----(i)

Again, doing cubes of both sides

⇒ (x + 1/x)3 = 125

⇒ x3 + 1/x3 = 125 – 3(5) = 110      ----(ii)

By (i) and (ii)

⇒ (x2 + 1/x2)( x3 + 1/x3) = 23 × 110 = 2530

⇒ x5 + (x + 1/x) + 1/x5 = 2530

⇒ x5 + 1/x5 = 2530 – 5

Required value: x5 + 1/x5 = 2525

Trick: 

If x + 1/x = k then the value of x5 + 1/x5 will always be equal to (k5 – 5k3 + 5k)

Here k = 5

x5 + 1/x5 = k5 – 5k3 + 5k = 55 - 5 × 53 + 5 × 5 = 2525

∴ Answer is 2525

After 2 years

Dividing (i) and (ii)

⇒ 51 = 1275R/100

So, rate of interest = 4%

questions.question: In triangle PQR, the sides PQ and PR are produced to A and B respectively. The bisectors of ∠AQR and ∠BRQ intersect at point O. If ∠QOR = 50°, then what is the value (in degrees) of ∠QPR?
questions.questionHtml: In triangle PQR, the sides PQ and PR are produced to A and B respectively. The bisectors of ∠AQR and ∠BRQ intersect at point O. If ∠QOR = 50°, then what is the value (in degrees) of ∠QPR?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

We know that the excenter of the triangle is the location where the bisectors of one internal angle and bisectors of two exterior angle bisectors of the opposite side of the triangle connect.

Here, O is the excenter

So, 90° - 1/2 (Opposite Angle) = Excenter angle

⇒ 90° - 1/2 × ∠QPR = ∠QOR

⇒ 90° - 1/2 × ∠QPR = 50°

⇒ ∠QPR = 2 × (90° - 50°) = 2 × 40° = 80°

Alternate Method

 

In ∆PQR

⇒ ∠QPR + ∠PRQ + ∠RQP = 180°

Now,

⇒ ∠QPR + (180 – 2 × ∠OQR) + (180 – 2 × ∠ORQ) = 180°

⇒ ∠QPR + 180 – 2 × ∠OQR + 180 – 2 × ∠ORQ = 180° (i)

In ∆OQR

⇒ ∠OQR + ∠QRO + ∠ROQ = 180°

⇒ ∠OQR + ∠QRO° = 180 - 50° = 130°

Multiplying by 2

⇒ 2(∠OQR + ∠QRO°) = 260° (ii)

Substituting (ii) in (i)

⇒ ∠QPR + 360° – 260° = 180°

⇒ ∠QPR = 80°

∴ the correct option is 3)

questions.question: The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph. P- To those who have known comfort, discomfort is a real torture. Q- Comfort is now one of the causes of its own spread. R- The more comfort is brought into the world, the more it is likely to be valued. S- It has now become a physical habit, a fashion, an ideal to be pursued for its own sake.
questions.questionHtml:
The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.

P- To those who have known comfort, discomfort is a real torture.

Q- Comfort is now one of the causes of its own spread.

R- The more comfort is brought into the world, the more it is likely to be valued.

S- It has now become a physical habit, a fashion, an ideal to be pursued for its own sake.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is ‘QSRP’.

Key Points

  • The given sentence is an example of a Sentence Jumble. 
  • The first statement of a sentence jumbled question is usually an independent general statement, a noun, a universal fact, the starting of an incident, or it starts with 'most' or 'once'.
  • Part Q will be the first sentence because it introduces the topic 'comfort'.
  • Part S mentions how comfort is turning into a habit and states the reason for comfort as one of the reasons for its spread.
  • Part R will be the next in sequence. Its mentions how comfort is turning valuable.
  • Part P mentions discomfort is the real torture for those who have taken comfort as a habit​

Paragraph after rearranging the sentences: Comfort is now one of the causes of its own spread. It has now become a physical habit, a fashion, an ideal to be pursued for its own sake. The more comfort is brought into the world, the more it is likely to be valued. To those who have known comfort, discomfort is a real torture.

Important Points

  • Important Rules to Solve the Para Jumbles:
    • Read the sentences attentively and try to comprehend the idea or theme of the paragraph.
    • Try to identify the opening and closing sentences of the paragraph. The sentence independent of the other sentences and introduces the new characters is generally the opening sentence. For the last sentence, look out for the sentence which can conclude the paragraph.
    • Try to identify the mandatory pairs. Two sentences can be connected through various connectors and other determinants.
    • Identify the pronouns which are connecting the sentences with each other.
    • Sometimes it is not necessary to identify all the sentences, we can arrange the sentences by eliminating the irrelevant option one by one.
